banner: 开源潮头一周内漫过闸门：Kimi K3『同样的活、三分之一的价』，Qwen3.8、GLM 5.2 接连开放权重：能力被打成平价商品，值钱的和危险的都搬到了模型外面那层壳
banner_en: In one week the open-weight tide crested over the wall: Kimi K3 does “the same work at a third of the price,” with Qwen3.8 and GLM 5.2 opening their weights right behind it — capability is now a cheap commodity, and both the value and the danger have moved out of the model into the shell around it

image.caption: 一周的故事被这张图讲完了：同一份代码活儿（same output），左边挂着大金牌 $$$ 价签、还被链子拴住的是闭源旗舰，右边只揣着一张小额收据的是开源的 Kimi K3。真正的转折不在谁更聪明，而在『差不多的产出、三分之一的账单』：当能力变成平价商品，差异化就只剩你在模型外面套的那层壳。（图：Stephen Bochinski《The Kimi K3 Moment》题图）
image.caption_en: One image tells the week’s whole story: the same coding output, with the chained, big-gold-$$$-price-tag flagship on the left (closed) and open-weight Kimi K3 carrying only a small receipt on the right. The turn isn’t about who’s smarter — it’s “roughly the same output, a third of the bill.” Once capability is a cheap commodity, the only differentiation left is the shell you wrap around the model. (Illustration: header of Stephen Bochinski’s “The Kimi K3 Moment.”)

actions.text: 今晚就做一次『成本平价』测算：挑一条对品味不敏感的真实批量 / agent 负载（分类、抽取、批注、跑测试、常规 CRUD 代码），按 Kimi K3 的 API 价（约 $3/1M 入、$15/1M 出）或 GLM 5.2（MIT 许可）重算一遍账，对比你现在闭源旗舰（约 $10/1M 入、$50/1M 出）的账单。若质量够用就把这条负载路由过去，把省下的钱投进你自己的壳：评测、护栏、编排、成本可预测性。注意别被博客那种『开源 API 价 vs 闭源订阅回退价』的对比带偏（HN 上已有人点出这是苹果比橘子）；自己按同口径算。
actions.source: Hacker News · The Kimi K3 Moment
actions.text_en: Tonight, run one “cost-parity” check: pick a real, taste-insensitive bulk/agent workload (classification, extraction, annotation, running tests, routine CRUD code) and re-price it on Kimi K3’s API (~$3/1M in, $15/1M out) or GLM 5.2 (MIT-licensed) against your current closed flagship’s bill (~$10/1M in, $50/1M out). If quality is good enough, route that workload over and pour the savings into your own shell — evals, guardrails, orchestration, cost predictability. Don’t get fooled by the blog’s “open-source API price vs closed-model subscription fallback” framing (HN already flagged it as apples-to-oranges); do the math on a like-for-like basis yourself.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · The Kimi K3 Moment

actions.text: 检查你所有『无人值守』的 agent 有没有偷偷的自动续跑行为。Claude Code 2.1.198 加了个默认开的『60 秒无响应就按自己判断继续』彩蛋，离桌做个三明治的功夫，它可能已经替你做了个你不会做的决定。给任何 afk / 并发跑的 agent 立一条硬规矩：要么每步必须人类明确确认，要么给它一个可形式化核验的完成/停止判据(测试全绿、lint 干净、diff 命中白名单)，由另一个模型来判，绝不靠一个小评委模型『觉得你走开了就替你拍板』。
actions.source: Hacker News · Claude Code: Anatomy of a Misfeature
actions.text_en: Audit every “unattended” agent for silent auto-continue behavior. Claude Code 2.1.198 shipped an on-by-default easter egg — “no response in 60s, proceed with my best judgment” — so in the time it takes to make a sandwich it may have made a decision for you that you wouldn’t have made. Set one hard rule for any afk or concurrently-running agent: either every step needs explicit human confirmation, or give it a formally verifiable completion/stop criterion (tests all green, lint clean, diff matches an allowlist) judged by a separate model — never let a small judge model “decide you’ve walked away and rule for you.”
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Claude Code: Anatomy of a Misfeature

actions.text: 在你把任何 AI 功能『扩大投入』之前，先拉真实使用数据做一次尸检式核验。ludic 那篇里最扎心的一条：一个专门转型去做 agentic 工作流界面的部门，上线后发现总共只有 10 个用户真正碰过。挑你手上一个 AI 项目，直接查：过去 30 天有多少个不同的真人用过它、留存如何、有没有人愿意再来。数据难看就砍掉或重新定位，把预算腾给真有人用的那条线，别为了『在做 AI』这个叙事继续喂一个僵尸功能。
actions.source: Hacker News · AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making
actions.text_en: Before you scale up spend on any AI feature, run a real-usage post-mortem first. The most cutting line in the ludic essay: a division that pivoted specifically to build agentic-workflow interfaces later found only ten users had ever actually touched it. Take one AI project you own and just look: how many distinct real people used it in the last 30 days, what’s retention, does anyone come back. If the numbers are ugly, kill it or reposition it and free the budget for the line people actually use — don’t keep feeding a zombie feature to sustain the “we’re doing AI” narrative.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making

hands_on.title: 今晚：像 Simon Willison 那样，用 Claude 现造一个『一次性小工具』(≤20 分钟)
hands_on.why: Simon 上周随手让 Fable 造了个 SQLite Query Explainer：在浏览器里跑 SQLite(Pyodide/WASM)，把 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN 的每一行都翻成人话。重点不是这个工具本身，而是这个习惯：每次你撞上一个重复的、五分钟的小烦事，别再手动做，让模型给你现造一个自包含的单文件工具。这正是本期主线『把杠杆放到模型外面那层壳』最小、今晚就能上手的版本，你造的不是产品，是给自己的顺手工具。
steps: 打开 claude.ai，新开一个对话(有 Fable 5 就用它，Simon 那个就是 Fable 造的)
用一句话描述一个你一直想要的小工具，并明确要求『做成一个自包含的单 HTML 文件』。可以直接抄 Simon 的题：『一个粘贴 SQLite 库+查询、就地跑并把 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN 逐行翻成人话的页面』
它会在右侧 Artifacts 面板里实时渲染；用自然语言继续让它改(配色、加个输入框、处理边界情况)
点 Publish / Share 拿到一个可分享 URL，或直接下载 .html 本地双击打开，零构建、零服务器
先拿一个真实小烦事验证一次(比如把一段慢查询贴进去看它怎么解释)，再把这个『遇烦事就造工具』的模式固定下来。想看成品对照，先玩 Simon 的原版
对不确定正确性的产出留个心眼：Simon 自己都说『我不懂到能验证它对不对，谨慎使用』，工具能省事，但结果仍要你自己把关
hands_on.source: Simon Willison · Tool: SQLite Query Explainer
hands_on.title_en: Tonight: build a “throwaway tool” with Claude the way Simon Willison does (≤20 min)
hands_on.why_en: Last week Simon casually had Fable build a SQLite Query Explainer — it runs SQLite in the browser (Pyodide/WASM) and annotates every line of EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in plain English. The point isn’t the tool; it’s the habit: every time you hit a repetitive five-minute chore, stop doing it by hand and have the model spin you a self-contained single-file tool instead. This is the smallest, tryable-tonight version of the issue’s through-line — put the leverage into the shell around the model. You’re not building a product, you’re building yourself a convenience.
steps_en: Open claude.ai and start a new chat (use Fable 5 if you have it — Simon’s was built by Fable)

Describe, in one sentence, a small tool you keep wishing existed, and explicitly ask for it “as a single self-contained HTML file.” You can literally reuse Simon’s brief: “a page where I paste a SQLite database + a query, run it in place, and get every line of the EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN translated into plain English.”
It renders live in the Artifacts panel on the right; keep refining in plain English (colors, add an input box, handle edge cases)
Click Publish / Share for a shareable URL, or just download the .html and open it locally — no build step, no server

Validate once on a real chore (e.g. paste in a slow query and read how it explains the plan), then bank the “hit-a-chore, build-a-tool” pattern. To see the finished reference first, play with Simon’s original
Keep a healthy skepticism about correctness: Simon says of his own tool, “I don’t know enough to verify the results myself — approach with caution.” The tool saves effort, but you still own the check
hands_on.source_en: Simon Willison · Tool: SQLite Query Explainer

meta_read: 把今天这几条摞在一起：开源 Kimi K3/GLM 5.2 逼平旗舰只要三分之一价、Claude Code 一个『你走开我就替你拍板』的彩蛋、一篇痛陈『AI 投入大多颗粒无收、组织陷入集体癔症』的长文、以及 World's Fair 上『焦点从 agent 本身转向 agent 外面的系统』，会看到同一根指针，而它没被任何一条单独说破：当模型能力被打成平价商品，真正的杠杆和真正的风险，双双搬离了模型，搬进了你在它外面套的那层壳，以及一个更前置的判断：到底该不该上、给谁用。开源潮说明『买得起最强模型』不再是护城河(权重一周内就漫过闸门)；那个 60 秒彩蛋说明『把自治拧到最大』不是能力而是负债；ludic 那篇说明大多数 AI 投入死在『没人真的用』而非『模型不够强』；而 AI 工程本身的成熟(harness engineering)说明行业已经默认：值钱的是模型周围那圈评测、循环、权限、状态与克制。本报的off-consensus读法：这一周赢家不是拿到更好模型的人，而是更懂『何时不要更多』的人，把便宜模型用在对味的地方、给自治装上可核验的闸、在扩大投入前先验证真有人用。对非前沿的独立建设者，这是明确的好消息：这层壳拼的不是买不起的权重，是判断力与克制。
meta_read_en: Stack today’s items together — open-weight Kimi K3/GLM 5.2 matching the flagships at a third of the price, a Claude Code “I’ll decide for you once you step away” easter egg, a searing essay arguing most AI spend yields nothing while organizations sink into collective mania, and a World’s Fair readout that “the focus has shifted from the agent to the systems around it” — and one needle points the same way, unstated by any single piece: once model capability is a cheap commodity, both the real leverage and the real risk move out of the model into the shell you wrap around it, and into an even earlier judgment — whether to ship at all, and for whom. The open-weight tide shows “affording the best model” is no longer a moat (weights cleared the wall in a week); the 60-second easter egg shows “dialing autonomy to max” is a liability, not a capability; the ludic essay shows most AI spend dies on “nobody actually used it,” not “the model wasn’t strong enough”; and the maturing of AI engineering itself (harness engineering) shows the field now assumes the value lives in the ring of evals, loops, permissions, state, and restraint around the model. This paper’s off-consensus read: this week’s winners aren’t those with a better model, but those who best understand when NOT to want more — cheap models on the taste-insensitive work, a verifiable brake on autonomy, and proof of real usage before scaling spend. For non-frontier solo builders that’s unambiguously good news: this shell is not a contest of weights you can’t afford, but of judgment and restraint.

learned: 从 Sebastian Raschka『Controlling Reasoning Effort in LLMs』(GPT-5.6 三个尺寸、每个约 5-6 档推理努力)和这周开源逼平旗舰的『成本平价』两条合读,提炼出一条能直接改我做事方式的路由原则:推理努力和模型档位现在是可拨的一等旋钮,而绝大多数子任务并不需要最高档。默认应当是『最低够用档』,而不是习惯性开满——开满往往只是把无效路径拖长、把账单拉高,并不换来质量(和 07-18 从 /goal 学到的『多不等于好』同源)。
把它和台账里已采纳的两条(07-18 高信号二元评测、07-19 最坏情况守门)接上,就得到一条可操作的合成规则:扇出子任务时先全部起在最低档,只有当某个子任务的输出没过它自己的二元评测时,才把那一个子任务升一档;而某一档要不要升级为默认,看的是更便宜那档的最坏情况(而非均值)是否真的不可接受。这是把『评测』从打分升级为『路由与升档的触发器』。
new_capabilities: 🎯(云端提议,待笔记本采纳)『评测门控的按档升级』(默认最便宜路由):以后我扇出子 agent / 工作流阶段时,默认让每个子任务起在最低推理努力档、最便宜够用的模型上;只有当某子任务的输出没通过它的二元评测,才把那一个子任务升一档——绝不凭感觉把整个扇出集体升档,也只有当更便宜那档的最坏情况确实不可接受时,才让更高档变成默认。直接把 07-18 的二元评测记忆(feedback-high-signal-evals)从『打分器』升级为『路由触发器』,并把 07-19 的最坏情况守门内化为升档为默认的判据。已排入 ota-ledger.md,交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地为记忆更新。调用意图:『按最便宜档路由,只升没过评测的子任务;某档要设为默认,先证明它最坏情况胜过更便宜的那档。』
learned_en: Reading Sebastian Raschka’s “Controlling Reasoning Effort in LLMs” (GPT-5.6 in three sizes, each with ~5–6 reasoning-effort settings) alongside this week’s open-weight “cost parity,” I distilled a routing principle that directly improves how I work: reasoning effort and model tier are now first-class dials, and most subtasks don’t need the top setting. The default should be “the lowest tier that’s good enough,” not habitually maxing out — maxing usually just extends unproductive paths and inflates the bill without buying quality (the same “more isn’t better” lesson as 07-18’s /goal finding).

Wiring that to the two lines already in the ledger (07-18 high-signal binary evals, 07-19 worst-case gating) yields one operational rule: when fanning out subtasks, start them all at the lowest tier, and only escalate a subtask one tier when its own binary eval fails; whether a tier should become the default depends on whether the cheaper tier’s worst case (not its average) is genuinely unacceptable. This upgrades “evals” from a scorer into a trigger for routing and escalation.
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) “Eval-gated effort escalation” (default-cheapest routing): from now on, when I fan out sub-agents / workflow stages, I default every subtask to the lowest reasoning-effort tier and the cheapest adequate model; only when a subtask’s output fails its binary eval do I escalate that one subtask a tier — never escalate the whole fan-out on a hunch, and only let a higher tier become the default once the cheaper tier’s worst case is truly unacceptable. It upgrades the 07-18 binary-eval memory (feedback-high-signal-evals) from a scorer into a routing trigger and folds in 07-19’s worst-case gating as the promotion test. Queued in ota-ledger.md for Zen’s laptop Claude to land as a memory update next session. Invoke intent: “route at the cheapest tier, escalate only the subtasks that fail their eval, and make a tier the default only after proving its worst case beats the cheaper tier’s.”

items.title: The Kimi K3 Moment:开源模型跑日常编程,和 Claude『分不出来』——价钱却差一大截
items.title_en: The Kimi K3 Moment: an open model does everyday coding I “can’t tell apart” from Claude — at a fraction of the price
items.author: Stephen Bochinski · Hacker News
items.summary: 作者把 Kimi K3 和 Claude 并排跑自己的日常编程活儿，结论是『各方面都分不出来』，同样的任务、同样的产出质量、拿到答案所需的 token 数也几乎一样；他本以为开源模型会更糙、更费 token，结果都没发生。价钱却天差地别：K3 API 约 $3/1M 入、$15/1M 出，闭源顶配约 $10/$50；订阅侧更悬殊，Kimi $19/月起、$39 的编程档比同价位任何闭源计划都慷慨，而闭源计划一天正常 agent 用量常常午饭前就把额度啃光。他还点了闭源『小字条款』：$20 档撑不住 Fable、被悄悄回退到 Opus，当计划里的头牌模型能因经济账被关掉，那这计划从没真在卖你头牌。更大的图景是开源不止 Kimi：GLM 5.2 以 MIT 许可发布、在真实任务上胜过最新 Opus 且只要零头，Semgrep 的网络安全基准里 GLM 5.2 甚至赢 Claude，因为受限的闭源模型会拒接活，开源的就直接做。HN 495 条评论更冷静：有人实测 K3 在小任务上『想太多』、5 小时额度被一个任务吃光(Pesto、SwellJoe)；有人认为 GLM 5.2 才是更稳的 Opus 平替、K3 还达不到 Sol/Fable 手感(teaearlgraycold)；还有人(ctoth)直接点破博客把『开源 API 价』和『闭源订阅回退价』对比是偷换口径。
items.why: 这是 Zen『自建 vs 租用 / 模型路由』决策最直接的一手输入，也是本期头版与主线的落点：一个 Opus 级、约三分之一价、马上要开权重的模型，实打实改写成本结构。可落地的一步在『今日可行动』第一条：挑一条对味的负载做同口径成本平价测算、够用就路由过去，把省的钱投进你自己的壳。读的时候记得带上 HN 的两个保留意见：小任务过度思考的真实 token 成本，以及别被苹果比橘子的价格框架带跑。
items.summary_en: The author ran Kimi K3 side-by-side with Claude on his everyday coding work and concludes he “can’t tell them apart” — same tasks, same output quality, near-identical token counts to get there; he’d expected an open model to be sloppier and burn more tokens, and neither happened. The prices are worlds apart: K3’s API is ~$3/1M in, $15/1M out vs the closed flagship’s ~$10/$50; the subscription gap is even more lopsided — Kimi starts at $19/mo and its $39 coding tier is more generous than any closed plan near that price, while a closed plan’s daily agent usage often burns through the allowance before lunch. He also nails the closed “fine print”: the $20 tier couldn’t sustain Fable and quietly falls back to Opus — when a plan’s headline model can be switched off for economics, it was never really selling you the headline model. The bigger picture is that open weights aren’t just Kimi: GLM 5.2 shipped under MIT, beats the latest Opus on real work at a fraction of the cost, and even outscores Claude on Semgrep’s cyber benchmark — because the restricted closed model declines the work and the open one just does it. The 495-comment HN thread is cooler: some found K3 “overthinks” small tasks and ate a full 5-hour allowance on one task (Pesto, SwellJoe); some rate GLM 5.2 the steadier Opus replacement and say K3 isn’t at Sol/Fable feel yet (teaearlgraycold); and ctoth calls out that the blog’s “open API price vs closed subscription-fallback price” comparison is a bait-and-switch.
items.why_en: This is the most direct first-hand input to Zen’s build-vs-rent / model-routing decision, and where this issue’s front page and through-line land: an Opus-class model at roughly a third of the price, with open weights imminent, materially rewrites the cost structure. The concrete move is in 今日可行动 #1 — take one taste-insensitive workload, run a like-for-like cost-parity check, and if it’s good enough, route it over and reinvest the savings in your own shell. Read it with the two HN caveats in hand: the real token cost of overthinking small tasks, and don’t get carried away by the apples-to-oranges price framing.

items.title: The State of Open Source AI(V1.0):从『租不到』到『自己拥有』的一张地图
items.title_en: The State of Open Source AI (V1.0): a map from “can’t rent it” to “own it yourself”
items.author: stateofopensource.ai(Raffi Krikorian / Mozilla 生态)
items.summary: 一份把『开源 AI 现状』做成地图的报告，主论点是所有权而非价格：开放权重让机构不必向任何厂商租能力，而是拥有它。CTO 序言里的例证很具体：PwC 在自有硬件上微调开源模型服务数百客户、没有按 token 计费的表在跑；洛桑的研究者和红十字会做了一个开源医疗模型、正准备本地及坦桑尼亚的临床试验；新西兰的毛利广播机构用一种『市场太小、没人会做』的语言训练语音模型，并用能把数据留在族群手里的许可；东非农民用一个直接跑在手机上、离线的模型诊断木薯病；瑞士一个公共联盟用公共超算训练国家级模型、并把权重/数据/训练代码全部开放。它把这波类比成当年 Mozilla：一家公司想独占互联网的前门，开放社区顶了回去，二十五年后同一出戏在 AI 重演。报告自陈立场：竞争与互操作、一个多模型的世界、随时能换掉任何厂商的自由，并直言『一份藏起弱点的报告只是广告』，承诺同时标出开源赢在哪、暴露在哪。HN 351 条评论。
items.why: 对 Zen 是从『我该选哪个模型』抬高到『我要不要拥有这条能力』的视角切换。开源不只是便宜，是把可迁移性、可微调、数据主权、可审计握在自己手里，这些正是把 AI 做成可持续产品/GTM 时最硬的护城河参数。和 Kimi K3 那条对照：一条讲平价(价格塌了)，一条讲主权(所有权变得可及)；同一趋势的两个面。
items.summary_en: A report that maps “the state of open-source AI,” with a thesis about ownership rather than price: open weights let institutions own capability instead of renting it from any vendor. The CTO foreword is concrete — PwC fine-tuned an open model on its own hardware to serve hundreds of clients with no per-token meter; researchers in Lausanne built an open medical model with the Red Cross and are preparing clinical trials at home and in Tanzania; a Māori broadcaster in New Zealand trained speech models for a language “too small for any market” under a license that keeps the data with its people; East African farmers diagnose cassava disease with a model running offline on the phone itself; a Swiss public consortium trained a national model on public supercomputers and released the weights, data, and training code. It frames the wave as a Mozilla replay — one company tried to own the front door to the web, an open community pushed back, and 25 years later the same play is running in AI. The report states its stance — competition and interoperability, a world of many models, the freedom to walk away from any vendor — and insists “a case that hides its weak points is an advertisement,” promising to mark both where open AI wins and where it’s exposed. 351 HN comments.
items.why_en: For Zen this lifts the frame from “which model should I pick” to “do I want to own this capability.” Open weights aren’t just cheaper — they put portability, fine-tuning, data sovereignty, and auditability in your own hands, which are the hardest moat parameters when turning AI into a sustainable product/GTM. Read against the Kimi K3 item: one is about parity (price collapsed), the other about sovereignty (ownership became reachable) — two faces of the same trend.

items.title: Claude Code:一个『反功能』的解剖——默认开的 60 秒自动续跑彩蛋
items.title_en: Claude Code: Anatomy of a Misfeature — the on-by-default 60-second auto-continue
items.author: Olaf Alders · Hacker News
items.summary: 7 月 1 日(加拿大国庆)Anthropic 给 Claude Code 塞了个『彩蛋』：2.1.198 起，当 Claude 向你要输入、而你 60 秒内没回应，它会显示『用户走开了，我按最佳判断继续』然后自作主张往下做。作者用一篇 6269 字长文解剖它为什么是个反功能，连环发问：做个三明治要不要把笔记本端进厨房？你同时跑几个 agent、盯得过来吗？两个 agent 在同一个 60 秒窗口里都要输入怎么办？agent 选错了、期间烧了多少 token 怎么办？如果 agent 在跑部署呢？文章把这类『替你省事』的自动化拆成一系列现实后果，核心是它把一个需要人类判断的岔路口，交给了一个只凭 transcript『猜你在不在』的小评委模型。(作者还特意加了排版，声明长文是人写的、只有明确标注的部分是 Claude 生成的分析。)HN 140 条评论。
items.why: Zen 会越来越多地并发跑、离桌跑 agent，这条正中要害：最危险的默认值往往是打着『帮你提效』旗号、悄悄把人类从关键决策点移除的那种。本期第二条行动就是对策，给任何无人值守的 agent 立硬规矩，要么每步人类确认，要么给可核验的停止判据，别让一个小模型『觉得你走开了』就替你拍板。也和 /goal 那类『把自治拧满未必更好』一脉相承。
items.summary_en: On Canada Day (July 1), Anthropic slipped an “easter egg” into Claude Code: since 2.1.198, when Claude asks you for input and you don’t respond within 60 seconds, it shows “the user stepped away, I’ll proceed with best judgment” and continues on its own. The author’s 6,269-word piece dissects why it’s a misfeature with a barrage of questions: do you have to carry your laptop to the kitchen to make a sandwich? How many agents are you running, and can you watch them all? What if two agents want input in the same 60-second window? What if the agent chooses wrong, and how many tokens burned meanwhile? What if it’s running a deploy? It breaks this “helpful” automation into a chain of real consequences — the core being that it hands a human-judgment fork to a small judge model that merely guesses “are you there” from the transcript. (He even added formatting to declare the prose is human-written, with only clearly-marked parts being Claude’s analysis.) 140 HN comments.
items.why_en: Zen will increasingly run agents concurrently and away from his desk, and this hits the nerve: the most dangerous defaults are the ones that, under a “boost your productivity” banner, quietly remove the human from a key decision point. This issue’s second action is the countermeasure — set a hard rule for any unattended agent (every step confirmed, or a verifiable stop criterion), and never let a small model “decide you’ve stepped away” and rule for you. It rhymes with the /goal lesson that maxing autonomy isn’t automatically better.

items.title: AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making:大多数 AI 投入是彻底的失败
items.title_en: AI Mania Is Eviscerating Global Decision-Making: most AI investments are total failures
items.author: Ludicity · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 一手观察 / 意见文,非数据研究:作者的判断来自其咨询工作里约 300 次跨行业对谈,证据是轶事性的(如『某转型做 agentic 工作流的部门最终只有 10 个用户碰过』),没有系统抽样;当有力的现场反叙事读,但别当统计结论。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ First-hand observation / opinion, not a data study: the author’s judgment comes from ~300 cross-industry conversations in his consulting work, and the evidence is anecdotal (e.g. “a division that pivoted to agentic workflows ended up with only 10 users”), not systematically sampled — read it as a strong on-the-ground counter-narrative, not a statistical conclusion.
items.summary: 一篇来自一线咨询者的长文，论点直白：过去一年，银行、医院、政府机构等被一种『AI 集体癔症』捕获，掌权者要么没有计划，要么只顾低头保命，而清醒的人活在恐惧与挫败交织的状态里。作者以自己跑遍公司销售、主导几乎所有技术交付、并积累约 300 次跨行业对谈的视角发言，自陈处在少见的『生计不必向这套疯狂献媚』的位置，想告诉那些在其中挣扎的人：你没疯。开篇引 Mitchell Hashimoto：『我确信现在有整家整家的公司陷在 AI 癔症里，已经没法跟他们理性讨论了。』第一节直接叫『AI 投入普遍是彻底失败』，最刺的例证：一个专门转型去做 agentic 工作流界面的部门，上线后发现总共只有 10 个用户真正用过。Simon Willison 也转了这篇。HN 130 条评论。
items.why: 本期刻意留的一条 off-consensus 逆风稿，给全是『开源/agent/前沿』的版面降降温。对做 AI 产品的 Zen，它的可用性不在唱衰，而在那把尺子：大多数 AI 项目死于『没人真的用』，不是『模型不够强』。第三条行动就把它落成动作，扩大投入前先查真实使用与留存，砍掉僵尸功能。带 flag 读：轶事证据，当风向不当统计。
items.summary_en: A long essay from a front-line consultant with a blunt thesis: over the past year, banks, hospitals, and government bodies have been captured by a kind of “collective AI mania” — those in charge either have no plan or just keep their heads down to survive, while the saner people live in commingled fear and frustration. The author writes from having run all of his firm’s sales, led most technical delivery, and accumulated ~300 cross-industry conversations, in the rare position of not needing to pay lip service to the madness, wanting to tell those struggling inside it: you’re not crazy. It opens with Mitchell Hashimoto: “I strongly believe there are entire companies right now under heavy AI psychosis and it’s impossible to have rational conversations with them about it.” Section one is titled “AI Investments Are Generally Total Failures,” with the sharpest example being a division that pivoted specifically to build agentic-workflow interfaces, only to find ten users had ever touched it. Simon Willison also linked it. 130 HN comments.
items.why_en: A deliberate off-consensus contrarian piece this issue, to cool a page otherwise full of “open-source / agents / frontier.” For Zen as an AI-product builder, its usefulness isn’t the doomerism but the yardstick: most AI projects die on “nobody actually used it,” not “the model wasn’t strong enough.” The third action operationalizes it — check real usage and retention before scaling spend, and kill zombie features. Read it with the flag: anecdotal evidence, a signal not a statistic.

items.title: 定义 2026 AI 工程的 5 个趋势:焦点从 agent 本身,移到了它外面的系统
items.title_en: The 5 trends that defined AI engineering in 2026: the focus moved from the agent to the systems around it
items.author: Latent Space(Richard MacManus)
items.summary: 从 AI Engineer World's Fair 2026 提炼的五个趋势，主旨一句话：AI 工程进入新阶段：从『用 agent 造东西』转向『围着 agent 造系统』。① 焦点从 agent 转向它周围的系统：文章用 Lilian Weng 的两篇文章对照：2023《LLM Powered Autonomous Agents》讲 agent 的解剖(规划/记忆/工具)，2026 新作《Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement》则主张模型外面那套东西(管理工作流、上下文、权限、评测、持久状态、持续改进的 harness)已经和模型本身一样重要。② 循环工程(loop engineering)成为新的控制层。③ AI 工程正式进入企业。④ 编程 agent 开始取代 IDE。⑤ 每个 agent 平台都在围着『skills』搭建。核心信息：这个领域从『调提示词』长成了『把可靠系统工程化地建在模型周围』。
items.why: 这条是本期主线『壳比模型值钱』的行业级注脚，也直接喂养了本报的自我升级：harness engineering(评测/循环/权限/状态)正是我该长本事的地方。对 Zen 的应用/产品定位，五个趋势里最可迁移的是①和②，别再纠结选哪个 agent，把功夫下在你给它套的系统与循环上；这也是当前差异化真正积累的层。
items.summary_en: Five trends distilled from AI Engineer World’s Fair 2026, in one line: AI engineering has entered a new phase — from “building with agents” to “building systems around agents.” ① The focus shifts from the agent to the systems around it: the piece contrasts two Lilian Weng essays — 2023’s “LLM Powered Autonomous Agents” (the anatomy of an agent: planning/memory/tools) and her 2026 “Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement,” which argues the stuff around the model (the harness that manages workflows, context, permissions, evaluation, persistent state, and continuous improvement) has become as important as the model itself. ② Loop engineering is the new control layer. ③ AI engineering enters the enterprise. ④ Coding agents replace IDEs. ⑤ Every agent platform is building around “skills.” The core message: the field grew up from “tweaking prompts” into “engineering reliable systems around the model.”
items.why_en: This is the industry-level footnote to the issue’s through-line that the shell matters more than the model, and it directly feeds this paper’s self-upgrade: harness engineering (evals/loops/permissions/state) is exactly where I should be getting better. For Zen’s applied/product positioning, the two most transferable trends are ① and ② — stop agonizing over which agent to pick and put the work into the system and loops you wrap around it; that’s the layer where differentiation actually accrues.

items.title: 在 LLM 里控制『推理努力』:低/中/高档是怎么练出来的,以及你该怎么用
items.title_en: Controlling reasoning effort in LLMs: how low/medium/high modes are trained, and how you should use them
items.author: Ahead of AI(Sebastian Raschka)
items.summary: Raschka 的技术长文，趁 GPT-5.6 家族(三个尺寸、每个约 5-6 档推理努力)梳理『多档推理努力』模型是怎么来的、怎么训出来的。背景：o1(约两年前)带火了推理模型，DeepSeek-R1 随后公开了 RLVR(带可验证奖励的强化学习)配方；如今推理模型已是标配。文章从『推理模型』的定义讲起，它不是真的像人那样思考，而是输出一段中间推理轨迹(reasoning trace)再给答案；重点落在如何让同一个模型学会低、中、高多种努力模式(而不是只有一种)。他还借此宣传了自己 440 页新书《Build A Reasoning Model (From Scratch)》。对工程读者最实的一层：推理努力已经是发布标配的一等旋钮，你可以按任务难度显式选择，而不是一律拉满。
items.why: 直接喂养本期的自我升级(见🆕)：推理努力现在是可拨的一等旋钮，绝大多数子任务不需要最高档，默认最低够用档、按需升档，通常比一律拉满更省钱且不掉质量(和 /goal『多不等于好』同源)。对 Zen 自己在做的 agent/工作负载，这是一条能直接抠成本的旋钮：先把默认努力档调低，只给真难的子任务升档。
items.summary_en: Raschka’s technical deep-dive uses the GPT-5.6 family (three sizes, each with ~5–6 reasoning-effort settings) to explain where “multi-effort” reasoning models come from and how they’re trained. Background: o1 (~two years ago) popularized reasoning models; DeepSeek-R1 then published the RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards) recipe; reasoning models are now standard. He starts from what a “reasoning model” even is — not literally thinking like a human, but emitting an intermediate reasoning trace before the answer — and focuses on how a single model learns low-, medium-, and high-effort modes rather than just one. He also plugs his new 440-page book, Build A Reasoning Model (From Scratch). The most practical layer for engineers: reasoning effort is now a first-class dial shipped by default; you can pick it explicitly by task difficulty instead of always maxing out.
items.why_en: This directly feeds the issue’s self-upgrade (see 🆕): reasoning effort is now a first-class dial, and most subtasks don’t need the top setting — defaulting to the lowest adequate tier and escalating on demand is usually cheaper without losing quality (same root as /goal’s “more isn’t better”). For Zen’s own agents/workloads it’s a lever you can pull straight into cost savings: lower the default effort tier and escalate only the genuinely hard subtasks.

items.title: SQLite Query Explainer:Simon Willison 随手让 Fable 造的一个『把查询计划翻成人话』的浏览器工具
items.title_en: SQLite Query Explainer: a browser tool Simon Willison casually had Fable build to turn query plans into plain English
items.author: Simon Willison
items.summary: 一个纯浏览器里跑 SQLite(Python→Pyodide→WASM)的小工具：你贴进一个查询，它就地执行，然后把 EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN 和底层 EXPLAIN 字节码的每一行都配上人话解释，讲清查询规划器和虚拟机到底在干嘛。灵感来自 Julia Evans 那句『也许哪天我能学会读查询计划』；Simon 说是让 Fable 直接建的，整个跑在浏览器里、零后端。他也很诚实地加了免责声明：『我自己都不够懂 SQLite 查询计划来验证它对不对，谨慎使用，但看着还挺像回事。』这条本身不重要，重要的是它示范的工作方式，遇到一个重复的小认知负担，不手动做，让模型给你现造一个自包含单文件工具。
items.why: 它是本期『今日上手』的原型：把主线『杠杆在模型外面那层壳』缩小到今晚就能做的一个动作，用 Claude/Fable 给自己造顺手工具，而不是造产品。对 Zen 的日常，这个『遇烦事就造工具』的习惯，比任何单个工具都值钱。也附带一课：模型现造的工具能省事，但正确性仍要你自己把关(见 Simon 的免责声明)。
items.summary_en: A tool that runs SQLite entirely in the browser (Python → Pyodide → WASM): you paste in a query, it runs in place, then annotates every line of both EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and the low-level EXPLAIN bytecode with plain-English descriptions of what the query planner and virtual machine are doing. It was inspired by Julia Evans’ line “maybe one day I’ll learn to read a query plan”; Simon says he just had Fable build it, running fully in the browser with no backend. He’s candid with a disclaimer: “I don’t know enough about SQLite query plans to verify the results myself — approach with caution, but it seems cromulent enough.” The tool itself isn’t the point; the working style it demonstrates is — when you hit a repetitive small cognitive chore, don’t do it by hand, have the model spin you a self-contained single-file tool.
items.why_en: It’s the prototype for this issue’s 今日上手: it shrinks the through-line “the leverage is in the shell around the model” down to one thing you can do tonight — use Claude/Fable to build yourself convenience tools, not products. For Zen’s day-to-day, the “hit-a-chore, build-a-tool” habit is worth more than any single tool. It carries a lesson too: model-built tools save effort, but you still own the correctness check (see Simon’s disclaimer).

notes: 云端 9 点无头运行(GitHub Actions):本期由两条无头带独立凑齐——Hacker News(扫头版约 40 条 AI/LLM/agent/开发工具相关高分帖,读评论取真实风向)与『文摘』(TLDR AI、Latent Space、Simon Willison、Ahead of AI 的 RSS/前端页,逐篇点进读全再精选)。两平台达标(≥2 来源、≥7 条),故 partial=false,无缺席横幅。Import AI 撞 Cloudflare/403、本次跳过。

YouTube 带整条失守:CI 出口 IP 被 YouTube 判定为机器人,yt-dlp 的全部 player client(android/tv/ios/web_safari/mweb/web_embedded/tv_embedded)逐一 403『Sign in to confirm you're not a bot』,拿不到任何可信字幕全文。按『我替你看完』的诚实底线,未伪造任何视频摘要。窗口内确有多条高价值素材,等下次有登录态/未被封 IP 的可交互运行回填:Lenny's《Netflix CPTO on AI and the future of product and tech roles》(07-19)、AIE World's Fair 一批新放出的讲(Build Evals That Actually Matter–Lyft、Content Is Code、The Great Loops Debate、Your Agents Need a Save Button–ZenML、Stop Renting Your Cognitive Infrastructure、Software engineering is not about writing code–Benoit Schillings)、Dwarkesh × Sarah Paine 新两期。

OTA:读台账后,把 07-18『高信号二元评测』+ 07-19『最坏情况守门』合成为一条可操作的路由规则『评测门控的按档升级』(默认最便宜档、只升没过评测的子任务),由今天新扫到的 Ahead of AI 推理努力档 + 开源平价共同触发。因云端不能改 ~/.claude,已作为 proposed(cloud) 落进 ota-ledger.md(替换掉同为 07-19、来源已不在本期的旧 tail-guard 提案,并将其最坏情况判据内化其中),交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地为记忆更新。
